text: A small board powered from a 2-pin header (5V, GND) that lights a red indicator LED at about 3 mA.
A USB-C power input board that exposes 5V and GND on a 2-pin header (5V, GND) and has a green power LED.
A board that takes 5V from USB-C and regulates it to 3.3V with a linear regulator. Break out 3.3V and GND on a 2-pin header (3V3, GND) and add a power LED on the 3.3V rail.
A breakout for an I2C temperature sensor. Power it at 3.3V from a 4-pin header (3V3, GND, SDA, SCL).
A voltage divider that scales a 12V input down to about 3.0V for a microcontroller ADC. Input on a 2-pin header (12V, GND), output on another 2-pin header (ADC, GND).
A pushbutton input for a 3.3V microcontroller. The output is high when released and low when pressed, with RC debouncing. Connect everything through a 3-pin header (3V3, GND, BTN).
A minimal 3.3V microcontroller board powered from a 2-pin header (3V3, GND), with a status LED on one GPIO and a 6-pin programming header (MISO, VCC, SCK, MOSI, RESET, GND).
A board with an I2C temperature sensor and an I2C EEPROM on the same bus, powered at 3.3V from a 4-pin header (3V3, GND, SDA, SCL).
A board that reads a humidity sensor over I2C, powered from USB-C through a 3.3V regulator, with a power LED. Break out the bus on a 4-pin header (3V3, GND, SDA, SCL).
A 3.3V microcontroller that reads an I2C temperature sensor and has a status LED. Power comes from a 2-pin header (3V3, GND).
A first-order RC low-pass filter with a cutoff near 1 kHz on an analog signal. Signal in on a 2-pin header (IN, GND), filtered output on another 2-pin header (OUT, GND).
A board powered from 5V with a power LED and two indicator LEDs, each switched by its own pin on a 4-pin header (5V, GND, LED_A, LED_B).
